Traupman 101

interest

verb: impersonal, from intersum; with meā, tuā or a genitive

it is in the interest of, it matters to

With the genitive of the person, or meā, tuā, nostrā, and an infinitive or a clause: illud meā magnī interest, tē ut videam (Cic. Att. 11.22.2, Lewis & Short), it matters a lot to me to see you. How much it matters goes in the genitive: magnī, permagnī, tantī.

Other words

  • rēfert — it matters (to me: meā)

    verb: impersonal · also used · classical · Phaedr. 1.15.9–10; Sen. Ep. 77.20: nōn quam diū, sed quam bene ācta sit, rēfert

    It makes no difference to me: nīl meā interest or rēfert (Traupman 96).

Examples

  • tuā et meā maximē interest tē valēre

    it matters most to you and to me that you get wellCic. Fam. 16.4.4

  • ergō quid rēfert meā cui serviam, clītellās cum portem meās?

    then what difference does it make to me whom I serve, so long as I carry my own packs?Phaedr. 1.15.9–10

See also interest, issue, business.
